# FinCorp — Q4 2025 Financial Report

**Reporting period:** October 1, 2025 – December 31, 2025
**Prepared by:** Finance Department
**Signed by:** John Smith, Chief Financial Officer
**Date of issue:** January 18, 2026
**Classification:** CONFIDENTIAL — Internal Use Only

---

## 1. Executive Summary

FinCorp closed Q4 2025 with total revenue of **$4.2M**, up 12% year-over-year. Operating
expenses grew to **$3.1M**, leaving a net operating income of **$1.1M**. Overall 2025 full-year
revenue reached **$15.8M**, beating the board target of $15M by 5.3%.

The quarter was marked by the successful onboarding of three enterprise clients
(Acme Bank, Meridian Holdings, and Kestrel Capital) and the completion of our SOC 2
Type II audit on November 24, 2025.

## 2. Revenue Breakdown

| Segment | Q4 2025 Revenue | % of Total |
|---------|-----------------|------------|
| Advisory Services | $1,850,000 | 44.0% |
| Asset Management | $1,420,000 | 33.8% |
| Compliance Consulting | $620,000 | 14.8% |

[S2] 1_Q4_2025_Financial_Report.md
| Technology Licensing | $310,000 | 7.4% |
| **Total** | **$4,200,000** | **100%** |

## 3. Operating Expenses

| Category | Q4 2025 Amount | Notes |
|----------|---------------:|-------|
| Payroll & Benefits | $1,820,000 | 58% of opex; headcount 94 |
| Technology & Cloud | $410,000 | Includes Horus deployment, $85K |
| Travel & Entertainment | $265,000 | See Expense Policy §3 for limits |
| Professional Services | $220,000 | Legal, audit, consultants |
| Facilities | $185,000 | Two offices: New York, Singapore |
| Marketing | $140,000 | Q4 trade show circuit |
| Other | $60,000 | |
| **Total** | **$3,100,000** | |

### Notable variances vs. budget

- **Travel & Entertainment** came in at $265K against a Q4 budget of $210K — a
  **$55K overage (+26%)**. Primary driver: three back-to-back client closings in Q4
  requiring in-person travel. Approval for overage signed by Sarah Johnson, COO,
  on December 12, 2025.

[S3] 1_Q4_2025_Financial_Report.md
- **Technology & Cloud** includes the initial Horus platform deployment and
  the ChromaDB infrastructure build-out.

## 4. Key Clients Onboarded in Q4

| Client | Contract Value (annual) | Start date |
|--------|------------------------:|------------|
| Acme Bank | $1,200,000 | Oct 15, 2025 |
| Meridian Holdings | $780,000 | Nov 3, 2025 |
| Kestrel Capital | $540,000 | Dec 1, 2025 |

## 5. Risks and Outlook

The primary risk flagged this quarter is regulatory: the upcoming **MiCA enforcement
in the EU on June 30, 2026** may affect our Singapore crypto advisory line. The
Compliance team, led by Michael Brown, is producing a mitigation plan due
**March 1, 2026**.

Outlook for Q1 2026: revenue target **$4.5M**, driven by a full quarter of Acme Bank
revenue and expansion of Meridian Holdings to advisory services.

## 6. Attestation

I certify that the figures in this report are accurate to the best of my knowledge
and have been reviewed by the external auditors on **January 14, 2026**.


[S4] 1_Q4_2025_Financial_Report.md
/s/ **John Smith**
Chief Financial Officer, FinCorp
January 18, 2026

# FinCorp — Employee Handbook

**Version:** 3.2
**Effective date:** January 1, 2026
**Owner:** Sarah Johnson, Chief Operating Officer
**HR Director:** Rachel Garcia
**Last reviewed:** December 15, 2025

---

## 1. Welcome to FinCorp

FinCorp is a financial advisory, asset management, and compliance consulting firm
headquartered in New York with a regional office in Singapore. Founded in 2014,
we serve over 80 enterprise clients globally. This handbook summarizes the
policies every employee is expected to follow.

## 2. Working Hours and Remote Work

- Standard working hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM local time.
- Hybrid policy: all employees are expected **in office at least 3 days per week**.
- Core collaboration hours: 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM local.
- Fully remote arrangements require written approval from the department head
  and from Sarah Johnson (COO).

## 3. Paid Time Off

| Tenure | Annual vacation days | Sick days |
|--------|---------------------:|----------:|

[S6] 2_Employee_Handbook.md
| 0–2 years | 18 | 10 |
| 3–5 years | 22 | 10 |
| 6+ years | 28 | 12 |

- Unused vacation may be carried over up to a **maximum of 5 days** into the next
  calendar year.
- Public holidays follow the local jurisdiction calendar.

## 4. Compensation and Benefits

- Salaries are reviewed annually, effective April 1 each year.
- Performance bonuses are paid quarterly, based on individual and company targets.
- Health insurance is fully employer-funded for the employee; dependents covered
  at 70%.
- Retirement contribution: employer matches up to 6% of base salary.

## 5. Expense Reimbursement

Expense reimbursement follows the **FinCorp Expense Policy** (see separate document).
Any expense above policy limits requires written pre-approval from the
employee's department head. Overages above $5,000 require approval from
**Sarah Johnson (COO)**.

## 6. Confidentiality

All employees sign an NDA on day one. Client data, financial figures, and

[S7] 2_Employee_Handbook.md
internal strategy documents are **strictly confidential** and classified per
the FinCorp Data Classification Policy (see Compliance Guidelines).

Violations can result in immediate termination and legal action.

## 7. Code of Conduct

FinCorp expects all employees to:

- Act with integrity toward clients, colleagues, and regulators.
- Report any suspected fraud, misconduct, or harassment to the HR Director
  (Rachel Garcia) or via the anonymous ethics hotline: ethics@fincorp.com.
- Comply with the Compliance Guidelines, including insider trading restrictions.

## 8. Termination

- **Notice period:** 30 days for standard employees, 60 days for senior managers,
  90 days for the executive team.
- Termination for cause (fraud, gross misconduct, NDA violation) is immediate.
- Exit interviews are conducted by Rachel Garcia within 5 business days of
  the notice.

## 9. Grievances

Any grievance should first be raised with the employee's direct manager.

[S8] 2_Employee_Handbook.md
If unresolved within 10 business days, it is escalated to Rachel Garcia.
Cases involving the HR Director are escalated directly to Sarah Johnson (COO).
